NEJM quote verbatim (abstract). Scott 2016 51% found verbatim in PMC4867749 full text. TOUCHSTONE NCT01647516 results posted 2020-10-14 as given. Downstream readout, within_2x reasonable.
Scott 2016 abstract sentence verbatim; regimen target opener, untested.

Tran 2017 quote verbatim. Europe PMC gives first publication 2017-04-11, not 2017-08-07 as the judgement says; year 2017 unchanged. Once daily also worked in TOUCHSTONE 2016, which could date it a year earlier.

738/446-fold quote and 2.4-fold HED sentence verbatim in the 216956 review. The note's 'without liver harm' is wrong: label 5.3 reports ALT >3x ULN in 4.5% vs 2.1% placebo (UC-1). 2 mg was tolerated, so same holds; fix the note.
Mizushima quote verbatim; Song 2008 quote verbatim (epub 2007-09-26). NCT01375179 confirmed TERMINATED, 27 enrolled, no whyStopped, no results.

Status right, field wrong: Scott 2016 full text states it: 'also consistent with preclinical disease model observations, RPC1063 induced clinical remission ... in patients with ulcerative colitis.' Set comparison_stated true (Scott epub 2016-04-28). Registry dates check out.
Sanna 2004 (JBC, epub 2004-01-19) quote verbatim in abstract.

Tran 2017 quote verbatim; FDA 209899 MedR S1P3 sentence found. Contra stands for the S1P3-KO model, but the filed monkey CV study (see missing) predicted the HR fall correctly, so the cell's best model changes in 2020.

IKACh quote, EC50 6x below Cmax, and -3.3 to -19.4 / -7.3 to -9.4 bpm all verbatim in the 216956 review. The study names etrasimod by its early code AR401959, so it may predate etrasimod FIH; still a retrodiction against fingolimod. Retro is defensible.

missing: Safety, model_change same, 2020, comparison_stated true, tier 2, imported_from MS (MONDO:0005301), model_filed true: FDA ozanimod Summary Review 209899 (2020) says 'The applicant provided data from a cardiovascular safety study in cynomolgus monkeys that demonstrated dose-dependent cardiovascular effects of ozanimod. Heart rate decreased by 20%...' and 'Reduction in heart rate and increased blood pressure are seen in patients treated with ozanimod.' The filed system predicted the bradycardia that the S1P3-KO mouse missed.

Safety, contra for etrasimod, 2023: dog CV safety pharmacology was silent (NOEL 350 mg/kg/day, FDA 216956 review) but patients' heart rate fell up to 19.4 bpm. The drafter mentions this only in a judgement. It is a different model (dog telemetry) and should be its own entry.
Efficacy patient_trials: NCT02447302 (etrasimod OASIS) has no DOI; Sandborn 2020 Gastroenterology doi 10.1053/j.gastro.2019.10.035. No change to status.
Searched for unreported UC failures of a member drug: none found. Ozanimod and etrasimod met their UC primary endpoints; mocravimod's UC phase 2 was terminated with no reason or results.
rule_questions: Decision 16 and margin_stated: the etrasimod NOAEL studies were IND-enabling (pre-trial), but the multiple at MRHD (738x/446x) is stated only in the 2023 review, after the trial. Does a pre-trial filed NOAEL count as a margin 'stated before the trial'?

Decision 16: the rat liver findings fell at >1000x MRHD, but patients at 2 mg had ALT elevations (label 5.3) that did not block dosing. Is that a misplaced-margin dose contra, a safety entry, or neither?
Can a retro entry (safety 3, model_change true) follow a contra and be drawn as the cell's latest status, or does a contra stand until a prospective prediction holds?

When the drafter's chosen model (S1P3-KO mouse, a design rationale in the literature) differs from the filed safety system (cynomolgus CV study), which one is 'the model the class relied on' for the safety cell, and do both get entries?

Scott 2016 was received Aug 2015, after the TOUCHSTONE topline (Oct 2014 press release), but the mouse colitis experiments probably predate the trial. Is a model paper published after the patient result a retrodiction when the experiments were run earlier?
